penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: A functional DOCX editor requires ongoing software engineering to maintain compatibility with the DOCX spec, handle edge cases, and fix rendering bugs — not automatable by Claude alone.

rationale: Building a reliable DOCX editor is a deep software engineering problem — OOXML is a notoriously complex spec and existing attempts (LibreOffice, OnlyOffice) have required years of engineering effort. This is not buildable by a Claude factory + simple tooling in any reasonable timeframe; buildability_with_ai scores 3 because it requires custom rendering logic, not prompts. The buyer mix is freelancers and indie devs who are motivated by avoiding a $100/year subscription, meaning price ceiling is very low and churn is high. The deciding factor is that this is fundamentally an engineering product, not a Claude-powered service, making it the wrong category for this factory.
solution_plan: WHAT: A hosted SaaS DOCX editor with basic formatting, track changes, and export. BUILD: This cannot realistically be built by the factory — a DOCX editor requires a rendering engine (e.g. integrating an existing open-source library like Mammoth.js or ProseMirror with OOXML serialization), which requires real software development, not Claude prompts. The operator cannot build or maintain this without a technical co-founder or contractor. SELL: N/A — build viability is the blocking constraint. MAINTAIN: N/A. REALITY CHECK: Do not pursue. The editorial opportunity here is reselling or white-labeling an existing editor (e.g. CKEditor, TinyMCE with DOCX plugin), but that involves licensing costs and integration complexity that still exceeds the factory's autonomous build capability.
notes: Total 3.2 — drop. buildability_with_ai (3) and operational_autonomy (4) both fail build_gates floors. This is an engineering product, not a Claude-powered service.
